description: Polls a Microsoft Teams channel for chat-requested job/asset runs and launches them -- but only for a requester already listed as an owner of the target.

teams_team_id.label: Teams Team Id
teams_team_id.description: Teams team id (Teams client -> team -> ... -> Get link).

teams_channel_id.label: Teams Channel Id
teams_channel_id.description: Teams channel id inside the team (e.g. '19:xxx@thread.tacv2').

oauth_state_dir.label: Oauth State Dir
oauth_state_dir.description: Local path or fsspec URI (s3://, gs://, abfs://) dedicated to this sensor's '.teams_oauth_state.json' -- holds a rotated OAuth refresh token, if Microsoft ever issues one. Without a durable place to persist it, the next rotation breaks this sensor's auth entirely.

triggers.label: Triggers
triggers.description: Phrase-to-target mappings this sensor recognizes. At least one required.

phrases.description: Case-insensitive substrings (unless case_sensitive_phrases=true) that identify this trigger in a message's text, e.g. ['run the nightly etl', 'kick off nightly']. The first trigger (in list order) with a phrase appearing anywhere in the message wins -- list more specific triggers first if phrases could overlap.

asset_selection.description: Materialize this asset selection when matched: explicit key list, the Dagster selection DSL (tag:/group:/kind:/boolean composition), '*', or a bare fnmatch glob -- resolved against sibling assets in the same defs folder. Owners are read LIVE from the matched assets' own `owners` catalog metadata; do not also set `owners` on this trigger.

job_name.description: Run this named job when matched, instead of an asset_selection -- for job-shaped targets with no asset metadata of their own (e.g. a job wrapping a bare op). Requires `owners` below: a bare job has no Dagster metadata to authorize against.

owners.description: Email addresses (or literal Azure AD object ids) allowed to trigger `job_name` from chat. Required when job_name is set -- there is no implicit default. Ignored for asset_selection triggers, whose owners come from the matched assets' own catalog metadata instead.

teams_tenant_id_env_var.label: Teams Tenant Id Env Var
teams_tenant_id_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD tenant id.

teams_client_id_env_var.label: Teams Client Id Env Var
teams_client_id_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD app registration client id.

teams_client_secret_env_var.label: Teams Client Secret Env Var
teams_client_secret_env_var.description: Env var holding the Azure AD app registration client secret.

teams_refresh_token_env_var.label: Teams Refresh Token Env Var
teams_refresh_token_env_var.description: Env var holding the INITIAL OAuth refresh token (one-time interactive consent for the dedicated bot account -- see this file's module docstring, 'Auth'). Only the seed; a later rotation is persisted to oauth_state_dir instead.

require_owner_authorization.label: Require Owner Authorization
require_owner_authorization.description: Require the message sender to be a listed owner of the matched target before launching it. THIS IS THE SAFETY CHECK THIS COMPONENT EXISTS TO ENFORCE -- setting it to false means ANY channel member can launch ANY configured trigger's target. Only disable it for a channel where every member is already trusted with every configured target.

resolve_requester_email.label: Resolve Requester Email
resolve_requester_email.description: Resolve the message sender's Azure AD object id to an email address via 'GET /users/{id}' (needs delegated User.Read.All) before checking owners -- most owners: lists use emails, not Azure AD object ids. When false, only a literal Azure AD object id in an owners list can ever match.

require_all_owners.label: Require All Owners
require_all_owners.description: For an asset_selection trigger matching MULTIPLE assets with different owners: false (default) authorizes the requester if they own ANY matched asset; true requires them to own EVERY matched asset. Ignored for job_name triggers (one owners list, not per-asset).

case_sensitive_phrases.label: Case Sensitive Phrases
case_sensitive_phrases.description: Match trigger phrases case-sensitively. Default: case-insensitive.

messages_per_poll.label: Messages Per Poll
messages_per_poll.description: Messages to request per Graph page (Graph's own hard cap is 50).

max_pages_per_poll.label: Max Pages Per Poll
max_pages_per_poll.description: Follow at most this many '@odata.nextLink' pages per poll -- bounds how far back a single tick can catch up after an outage.

process_backlog_on_first_run.label: Process Backlog On First Run
process_backlog_on_first_run.description: If false (default), the first-ever tick seeds the cursor to 'now' and processes nothing -- activating this sensor never replays a channel's past run requests. Set true only if that replay is actually wanted.

post_acknowledgement.label: Post Acknowledgement
post_acknowledgement.description: Reply in-thread when a match is authorized and launched, and (per on_unauthorized) when it's rejected. Needs delegated ChannelMessage.Send.

on_unauthorized.label: On Unauthorized
on_unauthorized.description: 'reply' (default) posts unauthorized_message_template as a thread reply; 'skip' just logs it. Ignored when post_acknowledgement is false.

ack_message_template.label: Ack Message Template
ack_message_template.description: HTML reply posted on an authorized match. Placeholders: {target}, {requester}, {phrase}. Give a list instead of a single string to have one chosen at random each time.

unauthorized_message_template.label: Unauthorized Message Template
unauthorized_message_template.description: HTML reply posted on an unauthorized match (on_unauthorized: reply). Placeholders: {target}, {requester}, {phrase}. Also accepts a list for a randomly-chosen reply.

default_status.label: Default Status
default_status.description: 'RUNNING' or 'STOPPED' -- initial status of the sensor.

match_dagster_links.label: Match Dagster Links
match_dagster_links.description: Also match a message that contains a link straight to the target asset or job in the Dagster UI (e.g. pasted via 'Copy link'), not just a typed phrase -- same owners-authorization gate either way. Recognizes the real dagster-webserver URL shapes: an asset's '/assets/<key-path>' (no location prefix needed) and a job's '/locations/<repoPath>/jobs/<name>' (or legacy '/pipelines/<name>'). Matching is by URL PATH SHAPE only -- it does not verify the link points at this Dagster instance, so a same-named target on a different deployment would also match; the owners gate still applies regardless.

skip_in_branch_deployments.label: Skip In Branch Deployments
skip_in_branch_deployments.description: Skip every tick while running inside a Dagster+ branch deployment (DAGSTER_CLOUD_IS_BRANCH_DEPLOYMENT=1). A branch deployment runs its own copy of every sensor alongside the full deployment's -- without this, a branch deployment double-acknowledges the same message and double-launches the matched job/asset selection.
